extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for revival of abandoned patent applications under 37 CFR 1.137 and related matters (intentional/unintentional delay, burden of proof, terminal disclaimers, provisional revival limits, public access, file handling, and interview policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional delay disqualifies revival under 37 CFR 1.137
rubrics_metrics.description: An intentional abandonment of an application, or an intentional delay in seeking the revival of an abandoned application, precludes a finding of unavoidable or unintentional delay pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An intentional delay resulting from a deliberate course of action chosen by the applicant is not affected by (A) the correctness of the applicant’s decision to abandon or not to seek revival; (B) the correctness or propriety of an Office rejection or decision; or (C) discovery of new information after abandonment. Deliberately delaying revival (for example, until industry or a competitor shows interest) is the antithesis of 'unavoidable' or 'unintentional' delay. See Application of G; Maldague.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe-harbor timing: petitions filed within 3 months and within 1 year
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office does not generally question whether there has been an intentional or impermissible delay when a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) is filed (A) within 3 months of the date the applicant is first notified that the application is abandoned; and (B) within 1 year of the date of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking revival are advised to file within 3 months of first notification of abandonment to avoid the question of intentional delay being raised by the Office or third parties. This is an operational safe-harbor, not an absolute entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to show 'unavoidable' or 'unintentional' delay when petition filed after 3 months
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) is not filed within 3 months of the date the applicant is first notified that the application is abandoned, the Office may consider there to be a question whether the delay was unavoidable or unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 1.137(a) petitions the Office will require a showing how the delay between first notification and petition filing was 'unavoidable'. For 1.137(b) the Office may require further information about the cause of the delay and how such delay was 'unintentional'. Applicants should include such showings to avoid delay in merit consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement when petition not filed within 1 year of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) is not filed within 1 year of the date of abandonment, the Office will require further information regarding when the applicant first became aware of the abandonment and a showing as to how the delay occurred despite due care or diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide (A) the date they first became aware of the abandonment, and (B) a showing how the failure to discover the abandoned status occurred despite exercise of due care or diligence by the applicant or representative (see Pratt). Failure to carry this burden may lead to denial regardless of original circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for 37 CFR 1.137(a) and (b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(a)(3) requires a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that the entire delay was unavoidable; 37 CFR 1.137(b)(3) requires a statement that the entire delay was unintentional (and the Director may require additional information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For petitions under 1.137(a) the applicant must carry the burden of proof that the entire delay from the due date until filing of a grantable petition was unavoidable. For 1.137(b) a statement of unintentionality is required; however the Director may demand additional evidence and may require the applicant to bear the burden of proof where questions arise (see Haines; Application of G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant party whose delay is evaluated
rubrics_metrics.description: The question under 37 CFR 1.137 is whether the delay on the part of the party having the right or authority to avoid abandonment (or to reply) was unavoidable or unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant assigned entire rights to a third party, the applicant's delay is irrelevant. If a third party (assignee, licensee, employer) controls prosecution, its decision whether to reply is binding on the applicant unless the contract expressly states the third party acts solely in a fiduciary capacity. See Kim v. Quigg; Winkler; Futures Technology Ltd. v. Quigg.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement under 37 CFR 1.137(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer (and fee) in certain categories of applications as specified in 1.137(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer required for: (A) design applications; (B) nonprovisional utility applications (other than reissue) filed before June 8, 1995; (C) nonprovisional plant applications (other than reissue) filed before June 8, 1995. Also required for utility/plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000 where abandonment occurred during appeal, interference, or secrecy order. Exceptions: revival solely for copendency with utility/plant filed on/after June 8, 1995, lapsed patents, reissue applications, or reexamination proceedings. Form PTO/SB/63 may be used when filing the terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer cannot substitute for showing unavoidable/unintentional delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a terminal disclaimer is not a substitute for establishing that the entire delay was unavoidable (1.137(a)) or unintentional (1.137(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer and the showing of unavoidable/unintentional delay are distinct requirements. A terminal disclaimer cannot excuse an intentional delay, nor will an unavoidable/unintentional delay waive the terminal disclaimer requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to waive terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.183
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who believes the terminal disclaimer requirement is inappropriate may petition under 37 CFR 1.183 for waiver of the 1.137(d) requirement (and pay the petition fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a petition must show an 'extraordinary situation' where 'justice requires' relief. The waiver may be requested in toto or to the extent the requirement exceeds the period considered appropriate by applicant. Example: abandonment caused no actual delay (e.g., application awaiting Board decision during abandonment). Grants are strictly limited to extraordinary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for request for reconsideration of refusal to revive (37 CFR 1.137(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application or lapsed patent must be filed within 2 months of the decision (or within such time set in the decision), unless the decision indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 unless the decision states otherwise. Renewed petitions or requests filed outside the specified time may prompt the Office to require a specific showing that the entire delay was 'unavoidable' (for 1.137(a)) or 'unintentional' (for 1.137(b)). Deliberate choice not to persist in seeking revival remains ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application revival limits (35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5) and 37 CFR 1.137(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application is regarded as abandoned 12 months after its filing date and shall not be subject to revival after such 12-month period; however, a provisional abandoned for failure to reply may be revived pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 for the 12-month period following filing if the delay was unavoidable or unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is permissible to file a revival petition later than 12 months, but revival can only restore pendency up to the 12-month period after filing. Even if granted, the provisional will not be pending after 12 months from its filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to abandoned published IFW applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Access will be provided to the application file itself for any non-Image File Wrapper (IFW) abandoned published application, and when IFW access is available via the File Information Unit and/or Internet such files will be provided accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since IFW applications may lack paper wrappers, if electronic access is unavailable the public may order a copy of the application-as-filed or specific documents from the Office of Public Records upon payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.19(b). See 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to abandoned unpublished applications when identified or relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to an abandoned unpublished application may be provided to any person if a written request for access is submitted and the abandoned application is identified or relied upon in certain documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification or reliance must be: (A) in a U.S. patent application publication or patent; (B) in a statutory invention registration; or (C) in an international application published per PCT Article 21(2). A copy may be provided upon written request and payment of the 1.19(b) fee. Form PTO/SB/68 may be used to request access under 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulling and forwarding abandoned application files to the Files Repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Files of abandoned applications are pulled and forwarded to the Files Repository on a biweekly basis one month after the full 6‑month statutory period has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abandonment date is after midnight of the date on which the set shortened statutory period (including any extensions under 37 CFR 1.136) expired. Examiners should carefully verify that files are actually abandoned and check for Board decisions with allowed claims to avoid erroneously sending files to the repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering patented and abandoned files (PALM/IFW procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patented and abandoned paper files are stored at the Files Repository or off-site warehouses; Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications are stored electronically and are the official record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners order files via PALM video display transaction by inputting location code, employee number, and patent/application numbers. The system responds with statuses (accepted; accepted but at off-site warehouse; not accepted—file not located; not accepted—previous request pending; not accepted—invalid number). Files are printed and processed daily; for IFW files electronic ordering/delivery is used and physical ordering is unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying applicants of abandonment and responsibility to maintain address
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Examining Corps mails a Notice of Abandonment (form PTOL-1432) to the correspondence address of record for applications that become abandoned for failure to prosecute; mere failure to receive the notice does not affect abandonment status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should promptly file a paper notifying the Office of any change of correspondence address in each application (except Customer Number practice) to ensure receipt of notices. Attention is directed to MPEP §§ 402 and 601.03 for address changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews must be conducted on Office premises and during Office hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners concerning applications and other matters pending before the Office must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours as designated by examiners; interviews at other times or places require Director authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews are permitted in examiner offices, conference rooms, or the Video Conference Center during normal business hours (Monday–Friday, excluding examiner overtime periods). The examiner may require that an interview be scheduled in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on interviews before first Office action for patentability discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview for discussion of the patentability of a pending application will not occur before the first Office action unless the application is a continuing or substitute application or the examiner determines the interview would advance prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits pre-examination patentability conferences; exceptions exist for continuing/substitute applications or at examiner discretion when it would advance prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement requirement after interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reconsideration is requested in view of an interview with an examiner, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview does not remove the necessity for formal replies to Office actions as specified in 37 CFR §§ 1.111 and 1.135. A written summary (Examiner Interview Summary Form or equivalent) must be placed in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet e-mail restrictions for interview-equivalent communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet e-mail shall NOT be used to conduct an exchange or communications similar to telephone or personal interviews unless a written authorization from the applicant or attorney/agent of record has been given to use Internet e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Internet e-mail is authorized for such exchanges, a paper copy of the e-mail contents MUST be made and placed in the patent application file as required by the Federal Records Act in the same manner as an Examiner Interview Summary Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Conference Center (VCC) procedures and PTRC use
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Video Conference Center (VCC) is available for authorized official business during normal hours and includes high-resolution document cameras, direct computer input, VCR display, and high-speed facsimile capability; PTRCs may also provide VCC services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customers wishing to use a PTRC should contact the desired PTRC to confirm availability and video-conferencing capability, identify two alternative dates/times for the video conference with both the examiner and the PTRC, and the patent examiner will coordinate arrangements via the PTRC Program Office. The customer will be notified of date/time by Office personnel.
